reason: This passage from Genesis 29-31 consistently portrays Yahweh (אֱלֹהִים/יְהוָה) as protective and beneficent toward Jacob and his family. Key evidence: (1) Yahweh opens Leah's womb in compassion (29:31); (2) God remembers Rachel and opens her womb (30:22); (3) Laban acknowledges Yahweh's blessing upon Jacob (30:27); (4) God speaks to Jacob in a dream commanding his return and promising 'I will be with you' (31:11-13); (5) Jacob testifies that 'the God of my father...has been on my side' and 'has seen my affliction' and protected him from Laban's harm (31:42); (6) God warns Laban in a dream not to speak harmfully to Jacob (31:24). Throughout, Yahweh actively blesses Jacob's labor, multiplies his flocks, protects him from Laban's schemes, and guides his journey. This demonstrates divine favor and protection, not antagonism.
